turns.message:
You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

---
name: continual-arc-actions
description: Solve Continual-ARC grid instances; choose demos, submit grids, and obey the evaluator's one-action JSON protocol.
---

# Continual-ARC actions

1. Parse the current task's grid, demo cap, and attempt/demo counts; keep all reasoning internal because the evaluator requires exactly one action JSON on the last line.
2. Compare each demo input/output to identify changed cells, preserved markers, and any spatial rule. Apply the rule to the test grid; check row/column counts and cell values before submission.
3. If multiple plausible rules remain, request a demo only when its expected clarification is worth the explicit cost and budget. Otherwise submit the best-supported grid; do not treat an unresolved guess as established.
4. On every turn, return exactly one permitted action object as the final line: request a demo, submit a grid, or finish only after the instance is over. Do not make unrelated tool calls or include prose that violates the task's response format.
5. After submission feedback, update the attempt count and use only the correctness signal; after demo feedback, incorporate that pair. Stop when the instance is over, then finish if required.
